findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the deploy/boot render step as a consumer of rebar.conf.template and specify the /mcp/ upstream include's fresh-boot behavior: use a zero-match-tolerant glob include (or have the render step seed a default upstream file) so `nginx -t` passes and nginx starts cleanly before foxterrier's first flip, mirroring the /opcert/ glob-include precedent the plan cites.
evidence: rebar.conf.template header: rendered via `envsubst '${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}'` in 'the deploy/boot script' — a consumer outside infra/nginx/

rebar.conf.template lines 30-34: the /opcert/ include is a GLOB `opcert-guard*.conf` 'precisely because nginx tolerates a ZERO-MATCH glob include (unlike a missing literal include, which is a config error): so on a FRESH boot with no materialized file, nginx STILL STARTS CLEANLY'

ABSENCE: the plan says the AC verifies `nginx -t` on the rendered template but does not say how the upstream-include file gets materialized on a fresh boot before foxterrier's first flip, nor whether a missing include fails `nginx -t`
findings.finding: The new /mcp/ location sources its switchable upstream from a 'materialized include' (the flip seam), but the plan does not enumerate the host-side deploy/boot render step (the envsubst that produces /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf per the template header) as a consumer that must also materialize/handle that include, nor state whether the include is zero-match-tolerant on a fresh boot — unlike the /opcert/ include the plan cites, which deliberately uses a GLOB include precisely so nginx STILL STARTS CLEANLY before the SSM-materialized file exists.
findings.location: Scope — infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template bullet; AC line 'The nginx /mcp/ upstream is a named block sourced from a materialized include ... verified by nginx -t on the rendered template'
scenarios: Fresh box boot / first render before any blue-green flip has materialized the upstream include: a missing literal include makes `nginx -t` fail and nginx refuses to start, taking down the whole TLS edge (gerrit + review + opcert), not just /mcp/
The render/boot step is not updated to emit a default upstream include, so the AC's `nginx -t` passes only in an author-primed local dir but not on the box
findings.suggested_fix: Model the upstream seam on the opcert guard-map: `include /etc/nginx/mcp-upstream*.conf;` (glob, zero-match-tolerant) with a committed default that points at the initial mcp loopback port, and name the render/boot script step that writes it, so a fresh boot serves /mcp/ against the initial container and foxterrier only rewrites+reloads to flip.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the CREATE step for the materialized upstream include: who writes its initial content and what default upstream target it carries so `nginx -t` passes and `/mcp/` routes on first boot before any foxterrier flip.
evidence: 'proxying to the MCP loopback port via a named upstream block whose target is a materialized include (the atomic-flip seam)'
AC: 'The nginx /mcp/ upstream is a named block sourced from a materialized include ... verified by nginx -t on the rendered template'
ABSENCE: the plan states foxterrier re-points the include but does not state who materializes its initial value or its default target
findings.finding: The nginx `/mcp/` upstream target is a 'materialized include' that foxterrier re-points atomically, i.e. shared state whose UPDATE (flip) is delegated. But this plan CREATES that state and does not define its initial content/creation: who writes the include first, what its default upstream target is, and what happens if the include is absent/empty when nginx first loads (nginx -t / reload would fail). The lifecycle CREATE step for the flip seam is under-specified.
findings.location: Scope — `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` 'a named upstream block whose target is a materialized include (the atomic-flip seam)'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the SIGTERM grace-window bound (value or config key/default) AND its ordering relationship to foxterrier's decoupled retirement — i.e. that traffic is flipped away and the container is only SIGTERMed when near-idle/retention-capped, so the grace is a residual backstop for ops present at retire time, NOT a gauge-gated drain that forces a kill on expiry (ADR 0104 §2).
evidence: Plan AC: 'sending SIGTERM while a long op is in flight lets it finish within the grace window before the process exits … not an immediate kill'

ADR 0104 §2 lines 78-81: a shared MCP server's 'in_flight gauge may never reach 0; a gauge-gated drain bound would then be exhausted and kill an in-flight certified op, and merely enlarging the bound only defers the same kill' — blue-green 'decouples retirement from the deploy'

ADR 0104 §2 step 5: retirement is 'gated by a flock-style still-serving? check … bounded retention, a hard retention cap' — i.e. the retire gate lives in foxterrier and traffic is flipped AWAY first, so the container's own grace is only a residual backstop

mcp_server.py has no SIGTERM/grace handling today — this is a net-new mechanism whose bound the plan does not name (contrast the review-bot's stop_grace_period 1320s derived from named budgets in docker-compose.yml lines 90-112)
findings.finding: The SIGTERM-grace mechanism's bound and its ordering relationship to foxterrier's decoupled retirement are unstated, so the AC as written ('lets it finish within the grace window before the process exits') reads as a bounded single-container drain — the exact gauge-gated-kill trap ADR 0104 §2 rejected for a shared MCP server whose in_flight gauge 'may never reach 0'.
findings.location: Scope bullet 'A /health endpoint … plus a bounded SIGTERM grace window'; AC 'SIGTERM grace'; Approach+rationale
scenarios: A retiring MCP container still handling several long LLM ops when SIGTERM lands: if the grace window is a fixed bound smaller than the residual op, the op is killed on expiry — reintroducing the kill the ADR's decoupling was meant to prevent
An implementer reads the AC literally and builds a self-drain-until-idle on the container, which under a never-idle shared server never exits and fights foxterrier's retention cap
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope/Approach note that the grace window is a bounded backstop for the residual op(s) present when foxterrier (having already flipped the upstream away and applied its still-serving/retention-cap gate) sends SIGTERM — name the grace value or its config key/default, and explicitly disclaim any self-drain-until-idle so the container's grace cannot force a kill under a never-idle shared server.
